seen_animation: A black-line side-view tractor (tall exhaust stack at upper left, rectangular body, small front wheel at lower left, large rear wheel at right with a rising line above it) sits small near the center of the frame in frames 1-8 against grey scenery: a horizon line, a zigzag of hills at upper right, two fence posts at left, and grass ticks along a ground curve. Across frames 1-8 it grows slowly and drifts slightly left; its rear wheel is a narrow upright oval. At frame 9 it is noticeably larger and the rear wheel starts to widen. Frames 9-12 it keeps growing and the wheel becomes rounder; the fence posts leave the frame by frame 12. At frame 13 it is larger again, filling most of the frame width, and frames 13-16 it settles at full size with the wheel fully round, matching the doodle's proportions.
seen_film: A tractor with a seated driver, towing a flatbed trailer, drives along a dirt road across flat open land toward the camera. In frames 1-8 it is small near the center, seen from a three-quarter front angle, and grows gradually as it approaches. At frame 9 it is clearly larger and is turning so that it is more side-on; frames 9-12 it keeps approaching and turning. At frame 13 it is larger again (with a doubled exhaust stack from motion blur in 13-14), and in frames 15-16 it fills the frame in near-profile, front to the left, large rear wheel at right, the trailer cut off at the right edge. A white post stands at the left edge through most of the shot.
named_subject: a tractor (side view: exhaust stack, body, small front wheel, large rear wheel)
evidence: Frame 1: animated tractor occupies roughly the same position and size as the film's (center-left, about a quarter of frame width). Frames 1-8: both grow by about 1.4x with the tractor staying near center. Frames 8 to 9: both show the same step up in size. Frames 12 to 13: both show the second step up, and in 13-16 both fill most of the frame width with front at left and large rear wheel at right. The narrow upright rear-wheel oval in frames 1-8 widening to the doodle's round wheel by frames 13-16 stands in for the film's three-quarter-to-profile turn. Frames 13-16 match c.png almost exactly.
primary_gap: The film's turn from a three-quarter front view to profile is carried only by the rear wheel narrowing; the body rectangle, stack and front wheel stay in flat profile throughout frames 1-12, so the turn does not read as a turn.
closes_when: In frames 1-8 the body rectangle is drawn foreshortened (shorter in width, with the front end slightly lower or angled toward the viewer) and opens out to the doodle's full rectangle across frames 9-13 at the same rate the rear wheel widens.
protect: The position and scale track (small center at frames 1-8, steps at 9 and 13, near frame-filling at 15-16), the stroke construction of c.png (open rectangle, hooked stack, cross-bar at the wheel, rising line, small rounded front wheel), the gradual wheel widening, and the sparse grey scenery style.
identity_gap: In frames 1-8 the rear wheel is squeezed into a narrow upright oval that is thinner than any wheel in c.png, but every other stroke matches the doodle and frames 13-16 are the doodle itself.
